runners_data.name: Chairmanfourtimes

runners_data.name: One And Gone

runners_data.comment: Had plenty of chances in handicaps but good 4th at Goodwood puts him on the scene

runners_data.name: Riley Rocks
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose 6f wins suggest he needs the strong pace to bring his stamina into play over 5f
runners_data.comment: Two 6f wins; coped well with 5f latest despite not getting a clear run; similar worry here
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins over 6f (on AW) but he didn't seem inconvenienced by the return to 5f, despite failing to get a clear passage, at Goodwood recently in the race won by Wedonttelllies; capable of better but he's come from off the pace in three of his four starts which will complicate things in this field.

runners_data.name: Naana's Shadow
runners_data.note: Prominent runner under Oisin Murphy who can press the pace without being part of the early burn
runners_data.comment: Improved as 3yo; useful front-running 3rd of 17 at York recently; in the thick of it again
runners_data.spotlight: AW winner as 2yo who has done well for new yard this year, making all from the rail draw at Catterick, then adopting the same tactics at York (5f, good) when losing her lead late on but still finishing a solid third of 17 (just ahead of Shes Got A Brother); in the thick of it.

runners_data.name: Temple Of Athena
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning to her favoured 5f trip where all three wins have come
runners_data.comment: All 3 wins at 5f; had excuses since the latest in March; return to 5f handicap should help
runners_data.spotlight: All three wins at 5f, on soft, good to soft and the AW; has had some excuses since the latest in March and the return to a 5f handicap looks in her best interests after she ran in Listed races either side of a modest 6f run at Chester; it's likely she needs to find extra for this, even so.

runners_data.name: U S S Charleston
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with decent recent turf form who can sit behind the early pace and finish
runners_data.comment: Appreciated soft ground when 5f winner at Yarmouth latest; up 7lb but rain helpful
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable rather than progressive on AW since a Wolverhampton win in December but he found soft turf to his liking when coming clear of his four rivals at Yarmouth (5f) last month; needs more off 7lb higher in this better race but further rain would help him more than some.

runners_data.name: Hanney Girl
runners_data.note: Front-runner with early speed but recent form suggests she may struggle to sustain pressure against stronger pace-setters
runners_data.comment: Two 5f wins as 2yo; creditable York run last month; will do well to win off current mark
runners_data.spotlight: Speedy filly who can lead; two 5f wins on good to firm as 2yo but she has run up to form on good to soft; creditable show when fifth of 17 at York last month but she will do well to win this off her current mark.

runners_data.name: Coyy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse under Saffie Osborne whose Windsor win showed he thrives when getting a strong pace to aim at
runners_data.comment: Cosy 5f winner at Windsor after met trouble; slowly away when creditable 3rd at Goodwood
runners_data.spotlight: Looked ahead of his mark when returned to 5f at Windsor (good to firm) in May, doing well to overcome a blocked passage, and a subsequent third behind Wedonttelllies at Goodwood (5f, good) after a slow start was creditable; has possibilities if he doesn't give himself too much to do.

runners_data.name: Proof
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose running style will suit the guaranteed strong gallop from the three confirmed leaders
runners_data.comment: Has won on heavy; won his return over 5f on AW; others likely to have brighter early speed
runners_data.spotlight: Heavy-ground winner as 2yo; started the year with a 5f Southwell AW win but the style of that success, when stamina finally came into play after he was niggled along from some way out, suggests others will have brighter early speed on the return to 5f; tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: Wedonttelllies
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse whose Goodwood win 13 days ago came from off the pace in similar circumstances
runners_data.comment: AW winner at 7f as 2yo but well suited by drop to 5f when Goodwood winner latest; up 6lb
runners_data.spotlight: All turf races have been on good or quicker but dam's best form was on soft; sole 2yo win was over 7f on the AW; ran well for a long way over 6f at Ascot on second run back and proved thoroughly at home over the new 5f trip at Goodwood (good; first-time cheekpieces) since, racing well within himself and coming clear for an impressive win; up 6lb but has better to come.

runners_data.name: Call Margot
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent turf form has been disappointing but the strong pace could bring out improvement
runners_data.comment: Overcame trouble in running for 5f win on AW in April; never involved back on turf at York
runners_data.spotlight: Did well to overcome trouble in running on Southwell AW (5f) in April but she wasn't in such good form at York (5f, good) three weeks ago in her first turf handicap; has something to prove after that.

runners_data.name: Henrythenate
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 28-day break whose best form has come with strong pace to chase
runners_data.comment: Three AW wins at 5f; creditable show at Chester for new yard; more on his plate today
runners_data.spotlight: Three 5f wins on AW for previous yards, most recently in February, but treading water in that sphere since; ran well for a long way at Chester (5f, good) in May for new trainer but has more on his plate in this company.

runners_data.name: Artista
runners_data.note: Prominent runner dropping into seller company recently whose form has declined markedly this season
runners_data.comment: Two 5f wins as 2yo; weighted to best this year; well beaten in a Beverley seller latest
runners_data.spotlight: Two 5f wins (good to firm and AW) last summer but she has been weighted to her best this year and was well beaten in a Beverley seller (first-time cheekpieces, now discarded) last month; up against it.

runners_data.name: Rosie Frith
runners_data.note: Front-runner carrying top weight whose form has been poor since returning from 33-day break
runners_data.comment: Front-runs; best form on AW; well held on Listed return; has work to do off this mark
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner; seems to handle most ground but her 5f maiden win at Cork (good to firm) last July was easily bettered by her AW achievements later; dropped right out on her return in a Listed race at Cork (extended 5f, soft) last month and has work to do off this mark back in a handicap.

runners_data.name: Alfa Duplicate
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best recent form has been on artificial surfaces rather than turf
runners_data.comment: Hung on to lead at Beverley latest; much bigger question to answer on very different track
runners_data.spotlight: Two AW wins at 5f/6f this spring; met her match in Call Margot at Southwell (5f, AW) in April but  showed her fighting spirit when refusing to give up her lead back on turf at Beverley (5f, good to soft) since; much bigger question here, up 4lb in a better race on a very different track.

races.paceDynamic: Shes Got A Brother, Rosie Frith, and Hanney Girl will ensure a scorching gallop from the start over this minimum trip. With three confirmed front-runners in a 16-runner field, the early pace will be fierce and unsustainable, creating carnage in the final furlong as the leaders tie up. The sprint will become a stamina test as horses with tactical pace who can settle and finish strongly will sweep past the spent pace-setters. This brutal pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses and prominent runners with a turn of foot over pure speed merchants.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If all three leaders go too fast and tie up badly in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The breakneck gallop will set up perfectly for horses like Wedonttelllies, Coyy and Proof who can settle off the pace and produce late kicks. Strong stayers with tactical speed will pick up the pieces as the front-runners fade dramatically.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-pressers can sit just behind the speed and kick
scenarios.body: Horses like One And Gone or Naana's Shadow who race prominently but not on the lead will benefit from the strong pace without being part of the early burn. They can track the leaders and strike when the front-runners weaken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one leader gets first run and holds on despite the pace
scenarios.body: Shes Got A Brother has the best recent form of the pace-setters and might steal a march if she can get first run on the rail. Her AW wins suggest she has the engine to sustain pressure better than Rosie Frith or Hanney Girl.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Meltdown
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so strong that a completely unconsidered closer wins at huge odds
scenarios.body: The three leaders could go suicidally fast, allowing a horse from the very back like Alfa Duplicate or Call Margot to come from nowhere. This would require an extreme pace collapse where even the prominent trackers get caught up in the early burn.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Shes Got A Brother to potentially get first run on the rail if she can break cleanest from the stalls
Monitor how aggressively Rosie Frith and Hanney Girl engage with Shes Got A Brother in the early pace battle
Check if Wedonttelllies can secure a clean passage from his draw to deliver his customary late challenge
Observe whether the three leaders go faster than even 5f specialists can sustain in the opening two furlongs
Watch for Oisin Murphy to position Naana's Shadow perfectly behind the pace battle without getting involved early

runners_data.name: Possessive

runners_data.name: Benefacta

runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner whose 5f speed may not translate to 6f stamina test, 30 days since last run could blunt sharpness

races.paceDynamic: Hickory Lad, Alpe d'Huez, and Time And Effort will ensure a strong gallop from the start, with Hickory Lad's proven 5f speed likely to see him lead early before the others join battle. The sustained pace over 6f on good to soft ground will create a thorough test of stamina, particularly as the field navigates Epsom's unique undulations. This relentless tempo will set up the race for the hold-up horses and those with proven stamina reserves. The combination of strong early pace and testing conditions clearly favours horses with closing kicks who can stay the trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three confirmed front runners maintain a strong gallop through the first 4f
scenarios.body: The pace will collapse in the final furlong, allowing hold-up horses with stamina to surge through and pick up the pieces. Late-running types with proven 6f+ form will have the perfect setup to showcase their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters can establish a decisive early lead and the others falter
scenarios.body: Hickory Lad's class edge could see him dictate terms and hold on, especially given his solid recent form and step up in trip. His proven speed combined with the softer ground may provide just enough stamina to resist late challenges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is merely strong rather than suicidal, allowing mid-division runners to stay in touch
scenarios.body: Horses racing prominently can position perfectly to strike when the leaders weaken, avoiding both the early burn-up and getting too far back. Those with tactical speed who can sit handy will have the ideal trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset from Unfancied
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves too strong for the fancied runners and opens up the race completely
scenarios.body: The testing conditions and strong gallop could bring stamina-laden outsiders into play, particularly those with unexposed profiles. Horses with question marks but proven staying ability might find this the perfect opportunity to outrun their odds.

watchPoints.text: Hickory Lad and Alpe d'Huez setting unsustainable fractions could collapse the entire front rank in final furlong
Time And Effort's modest form suggests she may not sustain the pace, potentially leaving the other two leaders isolated
Possessive breaking slowly from the stalls given his lightly raced profile and potential inexperience
Social Spirit and Dandyman Dan getting too far back early as strong pace could create impossible task from rear
Havana Flash's debut performance will reveal if breeding translates to immediate ability in this competitive heat

races.paceDynamic: Boiling Point will set the early gallop from the front with no genuine pace pressers in this small field, creating a sustainable rhythm through the early stages. Seagulls Eleven, Ice Max, and Chancellor will sit prominently behind the leader, while the two hold-up horses Skukuza and Persica will be anchored towards the rear. The lack of genuine early speed means this will develop into a tactical affair with a sprint finish from the top of the hill. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can position close to the pace and kick clear, rather than hold-up horses who will face a difficult task from too far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Boiling Point sets a steady pace and the prominent horses get first run
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows Seagulls Eleven, Ice Max and Chancellor to travel comfortably in behind before striking turning for home. Hold-up horses Skukuza and Persica are left with too much ground to make up in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Boiling Point gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear early in the straight
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows the leader to dictate terms and find extra when challenged, with the small field unable to close the gap. Prominent runners pick up the pieces but cannot reel in the winner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners engage in a pace duel from halfway
scenarios.body: Seagulls Eleven and Ice Max press Boiling Point harder than expected, setting up the race for Skukuza or Persica to stay on strongly. The tactical pace becomes more genuine, allowing the hold-up horses to be effective.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the favourites get into a speed battle or fail to fire
scenarios.body: The race becomes messy with positioning issues among the market leaders, allowing Chancellor or Royal Playwright to benefit from a cleaner passage. Their fresh conditions or improved form gives them an edge over tired rivals.

watchPoints.text: Boiling Point getting an uncontested lead could prove decisive given the lack of early pace in this small field
Skukuza and Persica need the prominent runners to go faster than expected to bring their stamina into play
Ice Max dropping back to handicap company after Group races could find this easier assignment
Chancellor's turf form unknown since switching to all-weather surfaces for recent improved displays
Seagulls Eleven's front-running tactics at Longchamp suggest aggressive intent from Oisin Murphy

runners_data.name: Tycoon
runners_data.note: Never raced on softer than good ground, creating significant going concerns despite recent improvement
runners_data.comment: Ran on well into a close third at Newmarket (1m1f, good to firm) last time
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on softer than good; failed to make a significant impact in his first four handicaps but did so at Newmarket (1m1f, good to firm) on latest outing, running on well into a close third of 12 off today's mark; return to 1m2f could help and he needs a second look.

runners_data.name: King's Code
runners_data.note: Struggled at Epsom previously and below form recently despite prominent style
runners_data.comment: Struggled to make an impact in recent AW starts and finished last on York return to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Below form in this race in 2024 and also last April on his only other visit here; had an excellent autumn last year on AW and won again in January, but he's struggled to make an impact in more recent AW starts and finished last at York on return to turf; return to 1m2f would suit if he were in better form but this may be a tough turf mark.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with proven soft ground form and Cesarewitch winner showing stamina for this distance
runners_data.comment: Not on a bad mark but plenty needs to go right if one of his late rushes is to prevail
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on good to soft, much more to prove on soft; won the Cesarewitch at Newmarket (2m2f, good to firm; 10lb higher today) last October and had some very solid AW form over 1m2f-2m this year, prior to tailing off at 50-1 in the Group 3 Ormonde at Chester four weeks ago; he's not on a bad mark but plenty needs to go right if one of his late rushes is to prevail in this.

runners_data.name: Sallaal
runners_data.note: Back to form last time with hood fitted and proven on soft ground from hold-up position
runners_data.comment: Upped to 1m2f for a C&D 2nd (good) on return, running on well with too much to do; up 5lb
runners_data.spotlight: Has run respectably on soft; hooded on last two starts, with a back-to-form second of six when stepped up to 1m2f for C&D handicap (good) on 2026 reappearance; raised 5lb since and probably not straightforward but that was a promising effort here from out the back (ran on well with too much to do) and he has to be in serious calculations.

runners_data.name: Alpha Crucis
runners_data.note: All four wins came on soft/heavy ground and twice runner-up at Epsom including this meeting
runners_data.comment: Stays 1m2f, has proved himself here and goes well in the mud; strong each-way claims
runners_data.spotlight: All four of his wins were on soft or heavy ground, three at Goodwood; runner-up on his only two visits here, including at this meeting (good to soft) last year and he's 1lb lower today; that was over 8.5f and his creditable fifth on reappearance ten weeks ago was in the 1m Lincoln at Doncaster, but he stays 1m2f; strong each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Quai De Bethune
runners_data.note: Unraced on softer than good conditions after 349-day absence raises fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Last-gasp win at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm); left A Balding for 775,000gns that July
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on softer than good; London Gold Cup third at Newbury last May was a promising start to handicap life and he built on that with a last-gasp win from out the back at Royal Ascot (again 1m2f on good to firm); unraced since, having left Andrew Balding for 775,000gns that July and been gelded in September; 7lb higher than at Royal Ascot but he's had just six races.

runners_data.name: Hand Of God
runners_data.note: Recent Newbury winner over this distance but limited experience on soft ground
runners_data.comment: Won by 2l going away at Newbury (1m2f, good) three weeks ago; unraced here or on soft
runners_data.spotlight: Won on good to soft in 2024, unraced on soft; lightly raced for his age but led in the final 1f of 11-runner race at Newbury (1m2f, good) three weeks ago and scored by 2l going away; back up 5lb; how he'll take to this new track and possible soft ground are greater worries but he makes appeal otherwise.

runners_data.name: Have Secret
runners_data.note: Visor fitted for first time and proven on soft/heavy ground from hold-up style
runners_data.comment: Career-high mark after April win; ran poorly in this last year on his only visit to Epsom
runners_data.spotlight: 6yo who has a career-high mark on the strength of his win at Pontefract (1m2f, good; acts on soft/heavy) in April; creditable fifth at York next time but the chief disincentive is probably that he ran poorly in this race last year on his only visit to Epsom.

runners_data.name: Ammes
runners_data.note: Fit from recent all-weather and hurdling but unraced on soft ground conditions
runners_data.comment: Good second of seven at Redcar (1m2f) five weeks ago, keeping on strongly; up 2lb
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on good to soft, unraced on soft; fit from AW and hurdling when good second of seven at Redcar (1m2f) five weeks ago, keeping on strongly; up 2lb and into a better race but needs a second look.

runners_data.name: Great David
runners_data.note: Won on soft as two-year-old but peak recent efforts have been on good ground
runners_data.comment: Ninth of 12 at Chester wasn't a greatly auspicious return to handicap; first headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Won on soft as 2yo; reappearance win last April saw him pitched afterwards into Listed and Group events, in which he was initially on the premises but his handicap mark shot up as a result; ninth of 12 to Respond at Chester wasn't a greatly auspicious return to handicap company on reappearance this season and connections now reach for headgear.

runners_data.name: Let's Dream
runners_data.note: Peak efforts on good ground with only one soft ground run producing poor form
runners_data.comment: Peak efforts have been on good going in the last 13 months; won at Chester on reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Won a soft-ground maiden in 2023 but peak efforts have been on good in the last 13 months; unraced here but scored twice over 1m2f at the similar Chester track, including on his only start this season; all three handicap wins were in tight finishes, but he's gone up just 3lb since latest and is likely to be seriously involved if he goes on the ground.

runners_data.name: Spoken Truth
runners_data.note: Highly competitive in recent 1m2f handicaps and proven on soft ground conditions
runners_data.comment: Acts on soft; highly competitive in 1m2f handicaps on all three starts for new connections
runners_data.spotlight: Rather disappointing for Dermot Weld in Ireland after winning a soft-ground maiden; has still not added to that 2024 win but he's been highly competitive in 1m2f handicaps on all three starts for new connections, runner-up to an unexposed rival in the Zetland Gold Cup at Redcar (good to firm) 11 days ago; each-way claims again.

races.paceDynamic: Liberty Lane will lead from the start with minimal early pressure, as most of this large field shows prominent or hold-up tendencies. Bolster, Respond, Tycoon and King's Code may settle in behind the leader, but none are aggressive early types. The soft going and 1m2f distance will create a steady gallop that builds gradually, with the real racing beginning only in the final 3-4 furlongs. This sustainable pace clearly favours hold-up horses who can produce late rallies, as the front-runners will lack the early pressure needed to soften up the closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Liberty Lane sets an uncontested lead through steady fractions
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows closers to conserve energy and unleash devastating finishing kicks, overwhelming the soft-pace leaders. Horses like Sallaal, Beylerbeyi and Alpha Crucis benefit most from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens notably from halfway as prominent horses press forward
scenarios.body: Respond and Hand Of God can capitalize on their tactical speed while the hold-up horses get caught in traffic or find insufficient pace to close into. The moderate tempo still allows these types to finish strongly without burning out early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Survive
scenarios.trigger: If Liberty Lane maintains his lead while the field fails to organize an effective challenge
scenarios.body: The soft ground saps the finishing kick from closers while Liberty Lane's stamina and early position prove decisive. Bolster could also benefit from tracking the winner throughout.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Liberty Lane stops quickly and no other horse takes up the running
scenarios.body: A complete lack of pace creates a sprint finish where any horse can win regardless of running style. The race becomes a lottery with tactical positioning mattering more than established profiles.

watchPoints.text: Liberty Lane could set fractions too slow for his own good if no prominent horses press him early
Tycoon and Quai De Bethune face significant going concerns having never raced on softer than good
Alpha Crucis has excellent Epsom form and all wins on soft/heavy, making him perfectly suited to conditions
Several hold-up horses including Dhahabi and Quai De Bethune return from lengthy absences exceeding 300 days
Sallaal wears a hood for the third time having improved markedly since this headgear was applied

races.name: Betfred Oaks (Group 1) (Fillies)

runners_data.name: Legacy Link
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to expected pace shape, Keane excels in Group 1s, excellent Gosden 14-day record
runners_data.comment: Asserted close home in the Group 3 Musidora at York and she's firmly in calculations
runners_data.spotlight: All four starts on good to firm/good ground; rallied for fourth in a hot running of the Group 1 Fillies' Mile at Newmarket last October on her final 2yo run, and she reappeared with a hard-fought win in the Group 3 Musidora at York (10.2f), asserting close home; there is every chance that she will stay 1m4f and her pedigree provides optimism that she will be effective on slow ground; dam is a sister to Frankel; firmly in calculations.

runners_data.name: Thundering On
runners_data.note: Prominent runner facing traffic concerns, improving profile suggests ready for Group 1 step, 41 days gap notable
runners_data.comment: Powered clear in 1m2f Group 3 at Navan in April when upped in trip; she's one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: By Frankel and dam won the 1m2f Group 1 Pretty Polly for connections; she's improved with each of her four starts and comfortably won the Group 3 Salsabil Stakes at Navan (1m2f, good to yielding) in April when upped in trip; has shown promise on heavy ground; powered clear in the final furlong last time, providing hope that she will stay 1m4f, and she's one to consider.

runners_data.name: A La Prochaine
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who could benefit from pace scenario, limited exposed form creates uncertainty in this grade
runners_data.comment: Still looked a work in progress when third to Amelia Earhart in Cheshire Oaks; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: She has an attractive German pedigree and was bought for 550,000gns as a yearling; won at Newbury (1m, soft) last October on sole 2yo start and beaten about 3l by Amelia Earhart when third in the Listed Cheshire Oaks at Chester (11.3f, good) on last month's reappearance; she still looked a work in progress last time (slowly away and outpaced turning for home) and could have lots more to offer; slow ground might aid her cause; interesting.

runners_data.name: Venetian Lace
runners_data.note: Prominent style faces traffic issues, unproven on slower ground despite one soft experience, Group 1 placed form solid
runners_data.comment: Rallied for 3rd in 1,000 Guineas and it's possible this sizeable step up in trip will suit
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 since debut win on AW last June and unproven on slow ground; however, she was a fine second in a red-hot running of the Group 1 Fillies' Mile at Newmarket last October and reappeared with an excellent third in the 1,000 Guineas there (1m) last month; made the running on her last two starts; by Derby winner Masar and rallied in the closing stages last time, so it's possible that this sizeable step up in trip will suit; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Sugar Island
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter gives her tactical advantage, proven on heavy ground, Whelan understands front-running tactics
runners_data.comment: Made all in 2yo Group 3 last October; work to do with two of these on Chester form
runners_data.spotlight: Third in Group 2 May Hill at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) last September and readily made all in Group 3 Staffordstown Stud Stakes at the Curragh (1m, heavy) in October; she could improve for last month's comeback run in the Listed Cheshire Oaks at Chester (11.3f, good) but has work to do with stablemate Amelia Earhart and A La Prochaine on that form; others preferred.

runners_data.name: K Sarra
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits race shape, drop back from 7f sprint distance aids stamina, Beckett's strong 14-day strike rate
runners_data.comment: Stayed on for third in the Musidora and could be a serious force over this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to connections' 10.2f/1m4f Group 2 winner Pride Of Arras; comfortable win at Southwell (1m, AW) last November on sole 2yo start and the drop to 7f was against her in the Fred Darling at Newbury (good) on her return; left that run well behind when staying on for third in the Group 3 Musidora at York (10.2f, good) last month, beaten just over 2l by Legacy Link; looks set to relish this step up in trip and she could be a serious force.

runners_data.name: Amelia Earhart
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in congested zone, Moore's tactical skills crucial, headgear addition suggests needed sharpening
runners_data.comment: Won the Listed Cheshire Oaks by 2l and is following same route as 2025 winner Minnie Hauk
runners_data.spotlight: Built upon previous promise (including on soft ground) when easily winning a maiden at Leopardstown (1m, yielding) last October on her fifth start, and reappeared with 2l win in Listed Cheshire Oaks at Chester (11.3f, good) where she wore a hood and blinkers for the first time (retained today); she's followed the same route on her last two races as Minnie Hauk, who won this for Ballydoyle 12 months ago, and Ryan Moore rides; major player.

runners_data.name: Cameo
runners_data.note: Prominent style creates positioning challenges, recent Lingfield win over extended trip encouraging for stamina test
runners_data.comment: Impressive in Lingfield trial; has a chance even though Ryan Moore rides Amelia Earhart
runners_data.spotlight: 7f maiden winner (soft to heavy) who took a big step forward with a convincing win in the Listed Oaks Trial at Lingfield (11.6f, good to firm) last month on her sixth start, which was her first run beyond 1m; Ryan Moore was on board last time and rides stablemate Amelia Earhart this afternoon, but she was certainly impressive at Lingfield and is unexposed at the trip; chance.

runners_data.name: On Message
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who could benefit from pace collapse, 13-day gap since last run keeps her sharp, proven AW performer
runners_data.comment: Strong finish for Listed third over 1m2f at Goodwood; might not be a forlorn hope each-way
runners_data.spotlight: Won Wolverhampton novice (7f, AW) last October on third start and followed up on handicap/seasonal debut here (8.5f, good) in April; kept on strongly for 1l third in Listed Height Of Fashion Stakes at Goodwood (1m2f, good) 13 days ago; she has plenty to find on form but the step up in trip could prompt further improvement and she might not be a forlorn hope each-way.

races.paceDynamic: Sugar Island sits alone on the lead and will dictate a measured gallop through the early stages without pressure. The real drama unfolds behind her where Thundering On, Venetian Lace, Amelia Earhart and Cameo all want prominent positions, creating inevitable traffic problems on Epsom's narrow track. This congestion will intensify from 3f out as runners fan wide around Tattenham Corner, with the pace likely quickening significantly in the final 2f. The sustainable early tempo followed by late acceleration strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the midrace squeeze and deliver late challenges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet get into each other's way from 3f out as expected
scenarios.body: The early steady pace allows closers to stay in touch while traffic problems eliminate several fancied runners. Legacy Link and K Sarra benefit most from clean runs and late kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner's Paradise
scenarios.trigger: If Sugar Island maintains her lead without serious pressure until the final 2f
scenarios.body: The uncontested lead proves decisive on a track that rewards bold front-running when the pace isn't fierce. Sugar Island's stamina background shows as others struggle to reel her in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Royal
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent quartet manages to secure an ideal position without interference
scenarios.body: The pace builds steadily from 4f out creating a true test of stamina where class tells. Venetian Lace or Thundering On use their Group 1 experience to best effect.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses to a crawl before a mad dash from 2f out
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace turns this into a sprint finish where positioning becomes critical. The race becomes a lottery with several runners having chances in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch for early scrimmaging between Thundering On, Venetian Lace, Amelia Earhart and Cameo as they jostle for prominent positions
Monitor Sugar Island's fractions through the first 6f - if uncontested she becomes very dangerous late
Observe Legacy Link's position turning for home as Keane often gets her settled deeper than ideal early
Check for any interference around Tattenham Corner where the prominent quartet will be bunched together
Watch K Sarra's response to pressure as she steps up significantly in class from maiden company

races.name: HKJC World Pool Handicap

runners_data.name: Mirsky
runners_data.note: Former winner of this race but 6lb higher this time and prominent style faces tactical challenge in large field
runners_data.comment: Won this last year off 6lb lower; won penultimate start and excuse latest; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: 7yo who was 6lb lower when landing this race (good to soft) last season; this year's running is more competitive but his success in the Thirsk Hunt Cup (1m, good to firm) last month was close to a career best and he had a possible excuse when failing to back that up at York; can't be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Popmaster
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with soft ground form but needs luck from wide draw in competitive handicap
runners_data.comment: Last effort, from poor draw, was better than it looks
runners_data.spotlight: Seven wins include three on good to soft/soft; also won on AW at Kempton (1m) in February but only midfield in valuable events at Newcastle (AW) and Ascot (good) on his last two starts; however, latter effort was better than it looks having been poorly drawn.

runners_data.name: Thunder Roar
runners_data.note: Soft ground specialist whose hold-up style is poorly suited to this likely pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Soft-ground specialist; down the weights & Colin Keane booking interesting; watch market
runners_data.spotlight: Soft-ground specialist who landed a fifth success when scoring at Ayr (1m) in September; yet to get going in three starts this year but he's edging down the weights and the booking of Colin Keane catches the eye; requires monitoring in the market with every drop of rain in his favour.

runners_data.name: Man Of La Mancha
runners_data.note: Progressive 4yo but hold-up style leaves him vulnerable to traffic problems in 18-runner field
runners_data.comment: Hampered latest; tactically versatile sort who is well drawn to sit handy; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded before winning at Windsor (good to firm) last May and finished that season with further wins at Sandown (also 1m, soft) and Newmarket (1m1f, good to firm); on the premises when he suffered chance-ending interference at Newbury last time and this tactically versatile sort is well drawn to sit handy; interesting.

runners_data.name: Ozat
runners_data.note: Ex-French import whose 48-day break and hold-up style create significant tactical disadvantages
runners_data.comment: Ex-French; 80-1 when down the field (1m, good) on his British debut
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French gelding who won four times there, the last two coming over 8.5f (AW) and 1m1f (good) at Chantilly last spring; changed hands for 75,000euros in November; 80-1 when 19th of 24 at Newbury (1m, good) in April on his British debut and he's probably one for further down the line.

runners_data.name: Bragbor
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs strong pace but likely scenario works against his running style
runners_data.comment: Useful on AW but only seventh on turf debut last time; plenty of guesswork involved
runners_data.spotlight: He made his debut only as a 4yo but it was a winning one at Newcastle (1m); subsequently useful form on AW included another narrow win at that venue (1m2f) in August for George Scott and he went mighty close over latter C&D on stable debut in November; niggled along at various stages when seventh on his turf debut (10.5f) last month and some guesswork is involved as to whether this test will bring out the best in him.

runners_data.name: Nizam
runners_data.note: Stablemate of Ozat with similar profile concerns plus 48-day absence and tactical positioning issues
runners_data.comment: Similar profile to stablemate Ozat; others look more likely
runners_data.spotlight: He has a similar profile to stablemate Ozat, boasting good form in France but 80-1 when down the field in that same Newbury race on his British debut; others look more likely.

runners_data.name: Sterling Knight
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore booking significant but hold-up style faces tactical challenge despite recent Newmarket win
runners_data.comment: Won 12th race when scoring last time; has never won off a mark this high, though
runners_data.spotlight: Versatile regarding ground and he was winning his 12th race when beating Jimmy Speaking and Final Night at Newmarket (1m, good) three weeks ago; that was a comfortable win and he has the assistance of Ryan Moore but this demands more from him (has never won off a mark this high).

runners_data.name: Jimmy Speaking
runners_data.note: Prominent style perfectly suits likely pace scenario and soft ground form is proven asset
runners_data.comment: Better than ever this season but he'll need more from this mark
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on soft ground; better than ever this season, winning at Doncaster (good to soft) and following up at Southwell (again 7f, AW); solid second to Sterling Knight (1m, good) last time but he'll need more from the same mark.

runners_data.name: Mister Winston
runners_data.note: Only genuine front runner gives massive tactical edge but unproven on going softer than good
runners_data.comment: Made all on return; not so good latest; unraced on softer than good but Murphy keeps faith
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on ground softer than good; Chester maiden (7.5f) winner who made all on Newmarket's July course last August; had been gelded when successfully repeating those tactics on his comeback at Newmarket (also 1m) in April but below that form back there at the Guineas meeting the following month; not dismissed, with Oisin Murphy sticking with him.

runners_data.name: Celeborn
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 340+ day break faces tactical and fitness concerns in large field
runners_data.comment: C&D winner; fair return and drops back in trip in cheekpieces; unexposed; he's a player
runners_data.spotlight: Won on good to soft as a juvenile and reappeared with good-ground C&D success at last year's Spring meeting; that was his only start in 2025 and he made a respectable comeback despite hanging when fifth of 11 at Newbury (1m2f) three weeks ago; drops back down in trip with cheekpieces added and his best days are almost certainly ahead of him; player.

runners_data.name: Principality
runners_data.note: Hold-up style poorly suited but has proven soft ground form and is dropping down in grade
runners_data.comment: Heavy-ground winner who won last time; 2lb nudge shouldn't stop him being competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Heavy-ground winner of a Glorious Goodwood handicap (1m) last July and he had dipped below that winning mark when scoring at Nottingham (8.5f, good) last time; 2lb nudge shouldn't stop him being competitive.

runners_data.name: Stem
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with soft ground form whose tactical style should benefit from likely pace collapse
runners_data.comment: Good second (1m, good to soft) on final start at three; respectable return; unexposed
runners_data.spotlight: Wide-margin win (7f, heavy) on his sole start at two promised plenty and, after being campaigned over 1m2f and 1m4f, he recorded a clear career best when second of 15 over 1m at Newbury (good to soft) on his final start at three; subsequently gelded and his reappearance when beaten less than 4l at Newbury in April was perfectly respectable; unexposed and he's respected.

runners_data.name: Walsingham
runners_data.note: Stablemate of Mirsky but hold-up style creates tactical problems despite trainer's course knowledge
runners_data.comment: It was this mark he raced from when well held at York three weeks ago; career best needed
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time winner who landed a third success at Pontefract (1m, good) on his penultimate start, having attracted support; also effective on a softer surface than that but it was this mark he raced from when well held at York three weeks ago and this demands a career best.

runners_data.name: Mr Swivell
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but inconsistent recent form and trainer's poor strike rate are concerns
runners_data.comment: Can go forward; has to put poor return behind him but that's not impossible
runners_data.spotlight: Proved progressive last year having joined this yard, winning three times (good to firm/AW) including when making all at Wolverhampton (8.5f) in July; also ran really well when second of 17 at Ascot (1m, soft; off current mark) in September but he was beaten a long way on his final start of that term and again at Lingfield on his reappearance four weeks ago; needs to put those efforts behind him but that's not out of the question.

runners_data.name: Hot Cash
runners_data.note: Prominent early but poor recent form including tailed-off effort creates serious reliability doubts
runners_data.comment: Course winner who was back near his best when second last time; far from dismissed
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on soft going; picked up a maiden here (7f, good) in July 2024 on his debut; fair run of form last year came to a crashing halt when virtually tailed off over C&D (good to soft) in September; subsequently gelded and he was back to near his best when second of 13 at Thirsk (1m, good) last time; far from dismissed.

runners_data.name: Asmen Warrior
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits scenario but yet to win for current yard despite multiple placed efforts
runners_data.comment: Soft conditions would ask a question but otherwise could go well in new headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Salisbury maiden (1m2f, good to firm) last June when sporting first-time cheekpieces for previous yard; yet to score for current stable but he's been placed on six of those seven starts and it was a narrow defeat when second of ten at Windsor (1m, good to firm; visored) under Silvestre De Sousa latest; soft going would ask a question but he's well drawn to go forward and newly fitted blinkers might eke out more.

runners_data.name: Final Night
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tactical disadvantages but low weight and improving AW form provide some hope
runners_data.comment: Good efforts on turf last two starts; career-high mark to overcome though
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time AW winner who is 0-6 on turf but his 40-1 second of 13 at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) was a good effort in May and he backed it up when third to Sterling Knight over that C&D (good) a fortnight later; sole start on good to soft (1m2f) last year was inconclusive but he'll do well to defy this career-high mark.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Winston is the lone confirmed front runner and will likely get an uncontested lead from the gates. With Jimmy Speaking, Stem, Hot Cash, Mr Swivell and Asmen Warrior all showing prominent tendencies, there's potential for early positioning battles behind the leader but no genuine pace pressure. The large field of 18 runners heavily weighted toward hold-up horses (Mirsky, Popmaster, Thunder Roar, Man Of La Mancha, Ozat, Bragbor, Nizam, Sterling Knight, Celeborn, Principality, Walsingham, Final Night) suggests a moderate tempo with the real race beginning from the 3-furlong pole. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can track the pace and kick clear before the hold-up brigade gets organized in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Winston gets soft fractions and isn't pressured early
scenarios.body: The 4yo gets first run on the field and uses his tactical advantage to score under Oisin Murphy. The hold-up horses get caught in traffic with too much ground to make up in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses engage Mister Winston from the 4-furlong pole
scenarios.body: Jimmy Speaking or Stem get ideal positioning behind the leader and have enough tactical pace to win the race to the line. Their recent form and going preferences give them the edge over the deeper-closing types.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a crawling affair
scenarios.body: Sterling Knight or Man Of La Mancha benefit from the tactical collapse and Ryan Moore's skill gets Sterling Knight into contention. The race becomes a pure sprint finish where class tells over position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the large field creates severe interference in the straight
scenarios.body: A horse like Popmaster or Ozat who gets a clean passage benefits from others' misfortune. The race becomes about luck rather than ability with an unconsidered runner taking advantage.

watchPoints.text: Mister Winston completely uncontested early - if he gets easy fractions he'll be very hard to peg back
Traffic problems inevitable with 18 runners - hold-up horses like Sterling Knight and Man Of La Mancha most vulnerable
Jimmy Speaking and Stem both showing prominent tendencies - watch for early positioning battle behind Mister Winston
Ozat and Nizam both returning from 48-day breaks for Ian Williams whose recent form is poor

races.name: Cygames Surrey Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Greek Mythology
runners_data.note: Front-running style suits the sharp Epsom track, progressive 7f form with 19 days freshening ideal
runners_data.comment: Thrice-raced Irish colt who has progressive 7f form; sire won on this card in 2019
runners_data.spotlight: Sire landed the Woodcote on this card in 2019 en route to even better things; this is a thrice-raced Irish colt who has progressive 7f form, most recently 1l third in Listed race at Naas (good); strong credentials.

runners_data.name: Ardisia
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with strong finishing kick, excellent going record and tactical pace will suit perfectly
runners_data.comment: Not totally solid on 2026 form and has probably already reached his ceiling anyway
runners_data.spotlight: Picked up a lot of prize-money during a busy 2yo season but isn't totally solid on 2026 efforts and has probably already reached his ceiling anyway; seems unlikely defy a 3lb penalty and top weight.

runners_data.name: Postmodern
runners_data.note: Aggressive front-runner returning from 91-day break, gelding operation may improve focus and determination
runners_data.comment: Has two useful pieces of 6f form; ready for a crack at 7f; hood is fitted
runners_data.spotlight: Has two useful pieces of 6f form, namely an emphatic domestic win on debut and rallying second in Meydan handicap last time; gelded since; ready for a crack at 7f; possibilities if taking well to first-time hood.

runners_data.name: Ten Carat Harry
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse thriving over 6-7f, recent turf win shows he handles these conditions well
runners_data.comment: Productive, mostly over 6f; has bits of 7f form, including at Listed level
runners_data.spotlight: Productive gelding, mostly over 6f and on AW; prevailed by a neck in Newmarket handicap (good to firm) back on turf last time, taking record to 7-12; has bits of 7f form, including at Listed level; in the mix.

runners_data.name: Stellar Sunrise
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid 7f form, disappointing last start can be overlooked in stronger company
runners_data.comment: Bit disappointing last time but otherwise a broadly progressive colt
runners_data.spotlight: Bit disappointing in similar event at Newmarket last time but otherwise a broadly progressive colt and can't be written off; ready winner of useful handicap at Newbury (7f, good) in his only other start this term.

runners_data.name: Ellusive Butterfly
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying 5lb claimer, traffic issues last time suggest better performance due
runners_data.comment: Has some encouraging turf form but this task demands a personal best
runners_data.spotlight: AW scorer; 0-5 on turf but ran well in this year's Fred Darling and looked better than the bare form (met traffic issues) in York handicap most recently; this task seems to demand a personal best, however.

runners_data.name: Awaken
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 51-day break, duck egg last start major concern despite previous Group form
runners_data.comment: Possible danger on these terms, provided she takes well to first-time hood
runners_data.spotlight: Ran well in Group events at Royal Ascot (6f) and Newmarket last season; posted a duck egg in the Nell Gwyn in sole run this term but looks a possible danger on these terms, provided she takes well to first-time hood.

runners_data.name: Northern Champion
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits, but 69-day gap and mixed record on home soil raises questions
runners_data.comment: Came up short in Group 1 last time when bidding for Meydan hat-tirck
runners_data.spotlight: Record is 3-6, most of those starts in non-domestic races; came up short in Group 1 last time when bidding for Meydan hat-trick; bit to prove back on home soil but very hard to dismiss on ratings.

runners_data.name: Assaranca
runners_data.note: Front-runner but significant class drop from handicap win, lowest official rating creates major disadvantage
runners_data.comment: Won well last time but has the worst chance at the weights back up in class
runners_data.spotlight: Won well at Lingfield (7f, good to firm) most recently but that was only a handicap off a mark of 70 and everything panned out perfectly for her; has the worst chance at the weights back up in class.

races.paceDynamic: Greek Mythology, Postmodern, and Assaranca will ensure a strong gallop from the start, with all three confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the early lead. The sustained pace over 7f on soft ground will test stamina reserves, particularly as Greek Mythology and Postmodern have shown they can maintain aggressive tactics. This tempo will stretch the field and create gaps, with the relentless gallop likely to find out any horse lacking staying power at the trip. The strong early pace clearly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses who can finish strongly, while pure speed horses and those needing things their own way will struggle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Greek Mythology and Postmodern engage in early battle with Assaranca tracking close
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will set up perfectly for late-running types who can unleash finishing kicks. Hold-up specialists like Ardisia and Ten Carat Harry will benefit most from the collapse of over-extended pace-setters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Greek Mythology gets loose on the lead without serious early pressure
scenarios.body: The progressive colt can dictate terms and kick clear turning for home before the closers can organize their challenges. His recent winning form over 7f gives him the tactical edge if allowed to control the tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Stellar Sunrise or Northern Champion track the pace perfectly without getting involved early
scenarios.body: They can position ideally behind the battling leaders and strike when the pace-setters weaken. Their class and tactical speed will prove decisive in a truly-run contest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too hard too early and all three fade dramatically
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish between mid-division horses who avoided the early fireworks. This would suit horses with natural speed who can quicken late without needing stamina.

watchPoints.text: Greek Mythology breaking smartly and establishing clear early lead without pressure could prove decisive
Postmodern's fitness after 91-day layoff and gelding operation - movement in betting will be telling
Ardisia's positioning in early stages - needs to be handy enough to launch late challenge
Northern Champion adapting back to domestic racing after Dubai campaign - market confidence crucial
Weather conditions if further rain arrives - already soft going could become testing for speed horses

races.name: Debenhams Handicap

runners_data.name: The Angel King

runners_data.comment: Step back in right direction when sixth at Chester; forecast slower ground could be a plus

runners_data.name: Rhoscolyn

runners_data.comment: Won this in 2021 and 2024 and this week's rain has been in his favour; dangerous mark

runners_data.name: Arctic Thunder
runners_data.note: Natural closer on a handy mark, recent Chester run suggests he needed a sharper track than tight turns
runners_data.comment: Chester may not have suited last time; he's on a handy mark on last season's best form
runners_data.spotlight: Not at the top of his game on either run this year but well backed at Chester last time, when the tight track may not have been ideal; on a handy mark on last season's best form and and he's not discounted.

runners_data.name: Dance In The Storm
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong 7f form but can be keen, Oisin Murphy booking significant
runners_data.comment: Won on reappearance at Chester despite wide draw; could still have more left in the tank
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo who can be difficult to settle but ran well in some quality handicaps last summer (including on good to soft; unraced on softer) and reappeared with a win at Chester (7f, good) last month; prevailed despite a wide draw and she could still have more left in the tank.

runners_data.name: Colombier
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning from long absence, French soft ground form excellent but fitness questionable
runners_data.comment: Pulled hard when well beaten on stable debut; interesting to see if his backers return
runners_data.spotlight: Won four times on slow ground in France (7f-1m2f); returned from long absence with heavy defeat on last month's stable debut at Ascot (1m, good to firm) where he pulled hard; that run may have got the freshness out of him and it will be interesting to see if he's again strong in the betting.

runners_data.name: Aurora Majesty
runners_data.note: Course winner last July, gelded since disappointing final 3yo run and drops the cheekpieces
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 4yo who twice ran really well over C&D last summer; could be involved
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointing last October on final 3yo start but the cheekpieces adopted that day are dispensed with and he's been gelded since; won over C&D (good) last July before very good efforts in defeat at Goodwood (7f, good to soft) and over C&D (good); retains potential and could be involved.

runners_data.name: Son
runners_data.note: Long winless run but recent runner-up efforts over 7f show he retains ability
runners_data.comment: On a long losing run and below par last time, but made good start for new yard previously
runners_data.spotlight: 0-17 since winning in June 2023 on his second start and he was below par at Newmarket (7f, good) three weeks ago; however, prior to that he was runner-up on his first two starts for this yard (7f, good) and has an each-way shout if he's back on song; has shown promise on good to soft ground.

runners_data.name: Monarch's Gold
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo stepping up in trip, strong Chester second suggests 7f will suit
runners_data.comment: Went close over 7.5f at Chester last month on first run beyond 6f; could be involved
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 3yo who went beyond 6f for the first time when going close at Chester (7.5f, good) last month; has also shown promise on good to soft ground; unexposed at this sort of trip and could be involved.

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: Stable change to O'Meara working well, recent Pontefract win shows he's in form
runners_data.comment: Got up close home over 6f on stable debut and could have more to offer; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Considerable promise during light career for Karl Burke and better than ever when getting up close home in small field on his stable/seasonal debut at Pontefract (6f, good); there can be optimism that he will be fine back up to 7f and on slower ground, and he could have more to offer; contender.

runners_data.name: Crimson Spirit
runners_data.note: Course specialist with two wins here, recent Goodwood success confirms current wellbeing

runners_data.spotlight: Two C&D wins, the latest when completing a hat-trick last July (good to firm), and he won at Goodwood (7f, good) a fortnight ago; could be bang there if handling the forecast slow ground (mixed messages in his form).

runners_data.name: Pietro
runners_data.note: Progressive type who won on AW return, hold-up style suits expected pace scenario
runners_data.comment: 4yo who has continued the good work this season and might not be far away
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive during last season's 3yo campaign and continued the good work when winning at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) in March on his reappearance; another good run when third to Dance In The Storm at Chester (7f, good) last month; versatile ground-wise and might not be far away.

runners_data.name: Sunny Smile
runners_data.note: Returning from 275-day break, talented but fitness major concern after long absence
runners_data.comment: Promising 2yo last year but this is a tough starting point to his 3yo year
runners_data.spotlight: Won 2yo maiden at Hamilton (6f, good) last July on third outing and runner-up there (6f, good to soft) in September on second nursery start; that latest form was franked by the winner and every chance he'll continue to improve, but this is a tough starting point to his 3yo year; cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Mister Bluebird
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner in excellent spring form, will ensure honest gallop throughout
runners_data.comment: 8yo who has been as good as ever this spring, runner-up on last two starts; respected
runners_data.spotlight: 8yo who has been as good as ever this spring, short-headed at Musselburgh (7f, good) then second of 14 to Crimson Spirit at Goodwood (7f, good); last season's two wins came on soft ground; effective here; respected.

runners_data.name: A War Eagle
runners_data.note: Made all at Beverley but needs career-best effort to win at this level

runners_data.spotlight: Made all at Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) in April on second stable start; respectable efforts when fifth on his next two outings but he needs something extra today and is unproven on slow ground.

runners_data.name: Musical Angel

runners_data.name: Zarathos

runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the 18th attempt at Windsor (1m, good to firm) last month and followed up in big field at York (7f, good) eight days later; latest 7lb rise may not stop this thriving 4yo if he handles the softer ground here.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Bluebird and Musical Angel will contest the early lead, with Mister Bluebird likely to get first run based on his recent front-running performances. The soft ground and 16-runner field will create a searching gallop, particularly with Dance In The Storm potentially adding pressure from a prominent position. The extended 7f trip on soft going will test stamina reserves in the final furlong, creating a setup where hold-up horses can close strongly. This pace dynamic strongly favours horses with proven finishing kicks who can settle off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Bluebird and Musical Angel engage early and Dance In The Storm adds pressure from prominent position
scenarios.body: The honest gallop stretches the field and creates perfect conditions for hold-up horses to unleash late runs on the soft ground. Arctic Thunder, The Angel King and Pietro benefit most from this strong tempo with their proven finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Musical Angel dictates alone with Mister Bluebird settling just behind rather than engaging
scenarios.body: A more controlled tempo allows prominent runners to keep closer tabs on proceedings and strike from better positions. Dance In The Storm and Veblen Good can position ideally while Zarathos benefits from his recent winning momentum.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Affair Benefits Class
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go steady early creating a sprint finish from halfway
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical battle where class and turn of foot matter most in the final 2f charge. Monarch's Gold can show his quality over this extended trip while Aurora Majesty benefits from the strong pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Leader Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If Musical Angel or Mister Bluebird steal significant early margins without serious pressure
scenarios.body: An uncontested leader can dictate terms and prove hard to peg back on the testing ground. Musical Angel's course winner status over this trip becomes crucial with her proven front-running ability.
